sources.citation: Tuinstra, Anna. 2019. Ipulo Phonology and Morphophonology. Yaounde: SIL Cameroon. 102 pp. (closest described relative, Central Tivoid B)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes Ipulo (not Caka) as a two-tone (H, L) language; a full-text search for stress/accent the text layer finds no statement on stress/accent. Mentions Caka [ckx] only as a neighbouring language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. [2016]. The Tivoid languages: Overview and Comparative Word List. Circulation draft, 16 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 3 'Phonology and morphology' (p.2) states 'For Tivoid languages, phonologies of any sort exist for only three languages, Tiv, Esimbi and Ugarə' and gives only tone information (Tiv, Ugare two-tone; Esimbi three tones). Table 1 (p.1) lists ALCAM (120-word list) as the only source for Caka [=Asaka]; Caka appears only as two wordlist columns (Batanga, Asaka).

sources.citation: Starr, Alan & Clark Regnier. 2008 [survey conducted 1990]. Tivoid Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-022. 52 pp.
